SellCraft AI — complete project blueprint
Tagline: One product photo. A few facts. A complete marketing kit.
SellCraft AI is an AI-powered content creation tool for small online sellers. A seller uploads product photos, enters a few verified details, chooses a platform and creative style, and receives a complete product listing plus a short video advertisement with optional AI voiceover.
The goal is to solve one repetitive, everyday business problem: small sellers spend too much time turning the same product information into good marketing content for different platforms.
The project fits the Side Hustle challenge because it targets a specific customer, produces something they can use immediately, and can use an open-weight language model as a core component.
1. Who are we building for?









Primary customer: Instagram sellers
Independent sellers of jewelry, accessories, gifts, handmade crafts, and home decor who repeatedly create product captions and promotional posts.











Secondary customers: Etsy and local product businesses
Sellers who need detailed listings, keywords, descriptions, promotional creatives, and reusable product content.



The first user should be one real seller with several products to list. They can test whether the generated copy is accurate, whether the video represents the product properly, and whether the result saves them time.
2. The complete user journey

Stage 1 — Add the product
Upload one or more product photos. Enter the product name, price, materials or ingredients, dimensions, features, benefits, and other facts. Fields should be optional where appropriate; do not invent missing information.




Stage 2 — Choose the creative direction
Choose Instagram, Facebook, Pinterest, Etsy, or Shopify. Select the writing tone, visual style, intended audience, and marketing objective.




Stage 3 — Generate the content
An open-weight language model creates platform-specific product copy and a structured video-ad brief. The video pipeline creates a 10-second MP4, and ElevenLabs optionally creates the voiceover.




Stage 4 — Edit and export
The seller reviews the results, edits or regenerates individual sections, previews the video, and downloads the finished assets.



3. What exactly does the AI generate?
The product should generate a complete marketing kit, not just a block of description text.
Asset    What the seller receives
Product title    Clear, platform-appropriate title
Short description    Concise product pitch
Full description    Formatted product-page copy
Feature bullets    Facts and benefits, grounded in supplied details
Keywords and tags    Relevant search phrases and platform tags
Social caption    A post written for the selected platform
Headline and CTA    A hook plus a clear call to action
SEO fields    Search title and meta description where appropriate
Video concept    Hook, scene sequence, motion prompt, and on-screen text
Voiceover script    Short spoken narration for the ad
Final video    A 10-second MP4, ideally vertical 9:16 for the first version
Optional voiceover    Audio generated through ElevenLabs and mixed into the video
The output changes based on the platform. An Etsy listing should not simply be an Instagram caption with different hashtags. Shopify should receive useful product-page content, while Pinterest should emphasize descriptive, searchable text.
4. Customization is a core feature
There should be a proper creative-controls panel.
Platform
Instagram
Facebook
Pinterest
Etsy
Shopify


Writing tone
Straightforward
Persuasive
Emotional
Friendly
Luxury
Playful


Visual style
Premium studio
UGC-style ad
Minimalist
Warm and cozy
Bold and colorful


Marketing goal
Drive sales
Brand awareness
Gift appeal
Explain features


We should also let users change just the tone and regenerate one section without losing the existing product details or regenerating the entire video every time.
5. The 10-second video-ad module
This is the feature that makes SellCraft AI stand out.
For the first MVP, use a consistent structure:
0–2s

Hook
Grab attention with a short line or an attractive opening shot.


2–6s

Product showcase
Show the product with generated motion or carefully animated camera movement.


6–8s

Key selling point
Display one verified feature or benefit.


8–10s

Call to action
Finish with the product name and a short CTA.



The video system has three separate responsibilities:
- Image-to-video generation: Use an open-weight model such as LTX-Video/LTX-2 through a suitable local or hosted inference setup. The official repository documents image-to-video support and identifies LTX-2 as its current generation of the model. 
  
  GitHub
- Audio generation: ElevenLabs generates the narration from the approved script using its text-to-speech API. Keep this optional and place its API key on the backend only. 
  
  ElevenLabs Documentation
  +1
- Video assembly: FFmpeg adds subtitles, verified text overlays, transitions, and audio, then produces the final MP4. 
  
  ffmpeg.org
Important: Real image-to-video generation requires suitable inference hardware or a compatible hosted inference service. If that isn't available, the app can create an animated-photo ad using the original product image. It must label this honestly as an animated-photo fallback, not pretend a video model generated it.
6. Technical architecture
I recommend a web application with a separate backend for model inference and media processing.
Next.js + TypeScript frontend
Product form, platform/tone controls, results editor, preview, downloads

Python FastAPI backend
Validation, generation jobs, API keys, file management, status reporting

Ollama + open-weight LLM
Copy and creative brief


Video provider
LTX-2 adapter or FFmpeg fallback



ElevenLabs TTS — optional
Narration audio, when configured

Final assets
Structured copy + optional voiceover + 10-second MP4 + download links


Recommended implementation choices:
Component    Choice
Frontend    Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui
Backend    Python, FastAPI, Pydantic
Open-weight language model    Gemma or another suitable instruction model through Ollama
Video generation    Modular image-to-video provider; optional LTX-2 inference
Fallback rendering    FFmpeg with gentle motion, overlays, and export
Voiceover    ElevenLabs API, optional
Local database    SQLite for job metadata
File storage    Local development storage with cleanup; configurable storage for deployment
Testing    Pytest for backend; frontend tests for key flows
Configuration    .env file locally, deployment secrets in the hosting platform
Gemma is one reasonable open-weight model family to evaluate, but check the specific model's applicable terms before distribution or commercial deployment. 

Google AI for Developers
+1



7. What makes the open-AI part meaningful?
The product should not be merely a frontend calling a closed AI API for every task.
The open-weight language model should actually control the core content generation: it interprets the product facts, follows the seller's creative choices, generates platform-specific copy, and produces a structured brief for video creation. Using a model adapter also makes it possible to change models later.
Be transparent in the README and challenge submission:
- Which model generates the product copy.
- Whether the model runs locally or through hosted inference.
- Whether product photos are sent to an external video provider.
- Whether ElevenLabs is used for narration.
- Which components cost money and which have local fallbacks.
Open weights do not automatically mean zero cost or unrestricted commercial licensing. Likewise, if the video provider is hosted, don't claim the entire pipeline runs offline.
8. Scope: what to build first
The four-day sprint should target one end-to-end workflow, not a complete SaaS platform.
Required MVP
- Upload a product photo and enter product facts.
- Choose a platform, tone, visual style, and marketing objective.
- Generate structured product copy with an open-weight model.
- Edit and regenerate copy.
- Generate a 10-second MP4 through an available video provider, or a clearly labelled animated-photo fallback.
- Optionally add ElevenLabs narration.
- Preview, download, and copy the outputs.
- Show loading progress and useful error messages.
- Include setup instructions and a real demonstration.
Do not build yet: user accounts, payment processing, automatic publishing to social platforms, a custom-trained model, analytics dashboards, a full product catalog manager, or ten different video generation modes.
Once a real seller confirms that the core workflow is useful, we can expand it.
9. Copy-paste prompt for your coding LLM
Use this with Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, or another coding agent. Open your project repository first and paste the prompt. It tells the agent to inspect the existing code before deciding what to change.
Build SellCraft AI — an AI marketing studio for small product sellers
Your role
Act as a senior full-stack engineer, AI engineer, product designer, and pragmatic technical lead. Build a functional, polished, end-to-end MVP of the product described below.
Do not only generate a plan, mockup, architecture diagram, or tutorial. Inspect the existing repository, implement the application, run the available checks, fix errors, and document how to run it.
If this is an existing repository, understand its structure and preserve working functionality. Do not overwrite files blindly. If it is empty, create the project structure.
When a model, API key, GPU, or external service is unavailable, implement a clear provider interface and an honest fallback. Do not fake successful AI generation or present placeholder media as genuine model-generated output.

1. Product definition
Product name: SellCraft AI
Tagline: One product photo. A few facts. A complete marketing kit.
SellCraft AI helps small online sellers turn product photographs and factual product details into ready-to-use marketing assets.
A user uploads a product photo, enters a few facts, chooses their sales platform and creative style, and receives:
1. A complete product listing.
2. Platform-specific marketing copy.
3. SEO/search metadata and relevant tags.
4. A short advertisement concept and storyboard.
5. A 10-second MP4 product ad.
6. An optional AI voiceover generated with ElevenLabs.
The target customer is a small seller on Instagram, Facebook, Pinterest, Etsy, or Shopify, especially sellers of handmade products, jewelry, accessories, gifts, home decor, and similar physical goods.
The product must solve a narrow, practical problem: creating marketing content repeatedly for the same products takes time, and generic AI copy often ignores the seller's tone or invents product claims.
The core promise is:
Enter product information once and generate a complete, editable, platform-ready marketing kit.
This MVP is an asset-generation tool. It does not automatically publish content to third-party platforms.
2. Required technology stack
Use this stack unless the existing repository provides a compelling reason to retain something else:
Frontend
- Next.js with App Router.
- TypeScript.
- Tailwind CSS.
- shadcn/ui or well-designed accessible components.
- Lucide icons.
- Responsive desktop and mobile layout.
Backend
- Python.
- FastAPI.
- Pydantic for request and response validation.
- SQLite for lightweight generation-job metadata.
- Local filesystem storage for development assets.
- Python HTTP client for external APIs.
- FFmpeg for video assembly.
AI providers
- An open-weight instruction model, preferably a Gemma model, accessed through Ollama for local development.
- A modular image-to-video provider interface. LTX-Video/LTX-2 is a candidate, but use a version and integration that are actually available and compatible with the environment.
- Optional ElevenLabs text-to-speech API for narration.
Do not place model inference, video rendering, or third-party API secrets in the frontend.
Use environment variables and create an .env.example containing placeholders, not real credentials.
Suggested configuration:
- OLLAMA_BASE_URL
- OLLAMA_MODEL
- ELEVENLABS_API_KEY
- ELEVENLABS_DEFAULT_VOICE_ID
- VIDEO_PROVIDER
- VIDEO_PROVIDER_URL
- VIDEO_PROVIDER_API_KEY
- UPLOAD_DIR
- OUTPUT_DIR
- DATABASE_URL
Use sensible local development defaults where possible.
3. Main user journey
Implement the following complete workflow.
Step A: Product input
Create a polished product-input screen containing:
- Product name — required.
- Product image — required.
- Short summary — optional.
- Price and currency — optional.
- Materials or ingredients — optional.
- Dimensions, size, capacity, or other specifications — optional.
- Main features — optional.
- Verified benefits — optional.
- Target audience — optional.
- Brand name — optional.
- Brand voice description — optional.
- Care instructions or usage information — optional.
- Claims or words that must not be used — optional.
Allow a user to preview the uploaded image, replace it, and remove it before generation.
Validate image types and file sizes on the backend. Support common JPEG, PNG, and WebP images. Reject invalid file types and unsafe filenames.
Do not require every field. The model must never invent missing specifications, prices, ingredients, certifications, or guarantees.
Step B: Creative settings
Create clearly organized, attractive selection controls.
Platforms
- Instagram.
- Facebook.
- Pinterest.
- Etsy.
- Shopify.
Allow one platform to be selected initially. Include a manageable option for generating content for all five platforms in the same request if the architecture permits it without duplicating video generation unnecessarily.
Writing tones
- Straightforward.
- Persuasive.
- Emotional.
- Friendly and conversational.
- Luxury or premium.
- Playful.
Visual styles
- Premium studio commercial.
- UGC-inspired social advertisement.
- Minimal and clean.
- Warm and cozy lifestyle.
- Bold and colorful.
Marketing objectives
- Drive sales.
- Build brand awareness.
- Gift appeal.
- Explain product features.
Video settings
- Default duration: 10 seconds.
- Default aspect ratio: vertical 9:16.
- Optional voiceover checkbox.
- Voice selection if ElevenLabs is configured.
Use actual buttons, radio controls, segmented controls, or dropdowns. Make the selected state visually clear.
Changing a creative setting should update the generation request. Do not implement decorative controls that do nothing.
Step C: Generate the marketing kit
When the user clicks Generate, validate the input and start a generation job.
Use asynchronous job status for long-running media generation. The user must not have to keep an HTTP request open while an image-to-video model runs.
Display clear progress states, for example:
1. Preparing product brief.
2. Writing product copy.
3. Creating video.
4. Generating voiceover, if enabled.
5. Assembling final video.
6. Ready to download.
Progress must reflect actual backend job states. Do not pretend a stage has completed when it has not.
Show meaningful errors and offer retry where appropriate.
Step D: Review and export
Display the completed content in a polished results workspace.
The user must be able to:
- Preview each generated copy section.
- Edit text directly.
- Copy individual sections.
- Regenerate an individual section.
- Change the tone and regenerate copy without re-entering product facts.
- Preview the video.
- Download the MP4.
- Download or copy the listing content.
- Download the voiceover audio if generated.
- See whether the video was generated by an image-to-video model or by the animated-photo fallback.
Do not force users to regenerate the video when they only change a caption.

4. Required copy-generation output
Use structured JSON output from the language model wherever possible. Validate the response using Pydantic. Handle invalid JSON and missing fields gracefully.
Generate these fields as applicable:
- product_title
- short_description
- full_description
- key_features
- benefits
- target_audience
- call_to_action
- seo_title
- meta_description
- keywords
- tags
- social_caption
- hashtags
- ad_headline
- voiceover_script
- video_hook
- video_storyboard
- video_generation_prompt
- missing_information
- claims_requiring_review
The response should also contain platform-specific output objects when multiple platforms are requested.
For Instagram, generate a hook, Reel caption, optional hashtags, and video on-screen text.
For Facebook, generate primary ad text, a headline, a description, and a CTA.
For Pinterest, generate a descriptive pin title, searchable description, and relevant keyword phrases.
For Etsy, generate a clear product title, detailed item description, relevant tags, and product attributes that are supported by the input.
For Shopify, generate product-page copy, feature bullets, an SEO title, and a meta description.
Treat these as editable templates, not promises of ranking or compliance with every current platform rule.
Copy-generation quality rules
The model must:
- Use supplied facts as the source of truth.
- Never invent product properties.
- Never invent discounts, scarcity, reviews, testimonials, awards, or customer results.
- Not assume a product is eco-friendly, organic, handmade, hypoallergenic, certified, or medically beneficial unless confirmed.
- Distinguish factual features from suggested marketing phrasing.
- Adapt tone without changing product facts.
- Keep calls to action appropriate for the selected platform and objective.
- Flag missing information rather than filling gaps with guesses.
Use a strong system prompt and structured generation schema.
Keep the generation prompt organized into product facts, selected platform, tone, style, objective, and output schema so that these concerns do not become mixed together.

5. Open-weight language-model integration
Create a dedicated backend service for language-model operations.
Use Ollama with a configurable open-weight model. Prefer a Gemma instruction model as the initial default, but allow a user or developer to change the model with configuration.
Do not hard-code model-specific response assumptions throughout the application.
The service should:
- Check whether Ollama is reachable.
- Check whether the configured model is available.
- Generate structured content.
- Parse and validate responses.
- Retry or repair malformed structured output when reasonable.
- Return understandable errors if the model is offline.
- Avoid leaking private prompts, product data, or secrets into application logs.
If Ollama is unavailable, show an actionable setup message. An optional deterministic demo mode may be provided to demonstrate the interface, but it must be visibly labelled as Demo Mode and must not claim to be a live model response.
The open-weight LLM is a core part of the product, not an optional decorative chatbot. It generates the actual marketing content and the structured brief for the media pipeline.
Keep the model provider behind a small interface so another compatible open-weight model can be substituted later.

6. Video-generation subsystem
Treat video generation as an independent backend service. Do not run heavy video inference in a Next.js request handler.
Create a provider abstraction such as:
- ImageToVideoProvider
- OpenWeightImageToVideoProvider
- AnimatedPhotoFallbackProvider
The provider must accept:
- An input product image.
- A motion prompt.
- Desired duration.
- Desired aspect ratio.
- An output location or job context.
It must return a validated media path or a clear error.
Preferred real image-to-video mode
Support a genuine image-to-video model when an actual inference endpoint or compatible local model environment is configured.
LTX-Video/LTX-2 can be evaluated first. Before claiming the integration works, verify the actual model version, weights, licensing terms, invocation method, hardware requirements, and output format.
Do not invent an unofficial API contract. Implement the adapter for the real runtime or inference endpoint being used, and document its configuration.
The motion prompt should:
- Describe camera movement and subtle scene motion.
- Keep the product's defining appearance as consistent as possible.
- Avoid creating fake labels, fake logos, or invented product details.
- Avoid changes that materially misrepresent the product.
Do not ask the image-to-video model to render important titles or precise CTA text. Add typography during the final assembly step.
Animated-photo fallback
When no compatible image-to-video runtime is configured, create a legitimate 10-second MP4 from the uploaded product image using FFmpeg.
Support:
- Subtle zoom and pan.
- Appropriate crop and framing.
- A clean background or solid-color canvas when appropriate.
- Professionally placed text overlays.
- A hook, one verified feature, and a CTA.
- Optional narration audio.
- Captions/subtitles if available.
The fallback must be visually polished, not a raw still image placed inside a video container.
The UI and API response must clearly label this output as an animated-photo ad, not AI-generated motion footage.
Both the real model and fallback paths should produce an actual playable MP4 file with a verified duration of approximately 10 seconds.
Use FFprobe or equivalent validation to check the final file and fail the job if export fails.

7. ElevenLabs voiceover integration
Implement an optional ElevenLabs text-to-speech service.
Requirements:
- Use the official API and its documented request format.
- Store API credentials exclusively on the backend.
- Generate narration from the approved voiceover_script.
- Allow the configured voice to be selected from available permitted voices.
- Support the output audio format required for video assembly.
- Handle authentication, rate limits, quota limits, timeouts, and API errors.
- Make the voiceover feature optional.
If no ElevenLabs API key is configured:
- Keep the text script visible and editable.
- Let the user create a silent video with subtitles or on-screen copy.
- Display a clear message explaining that voice generation requires configuration.
- Do not create fake narration or claim the voice was generated.
Do not include voice cloning of a real person as part of this MVP.
If voiceover is enabled, estimate whether the script will fit a 10-second ad. Avoid excessively long narration. Let the user edit the script and regenerate the audio if necessary.

8. Final video assembly
Use FFmpeg to assemble the final video.
The assembly pipeline should:
1. Receive the generated footage or animated-photo clip.
2. Normalize duration, dimensions, frame rate, and codec as needed.
3. Add accurate, readable text overlays.
4. Add captions or subtitles when appropriate.
5. Mix in the generated narration if available.
6. Add background audio only when it is licensed or otherwise appropriate for use.
7. Normalize audio levels.
8. Export an MP4 with H.264 video and a widely supported audio codec when audio is present.
9. Validate output duration and media readability.
10. Return a downloadable asset.
Default to vertical 9:16 output, but keep dimensions configurable.
Do not stretch source images incorrectly. Maintain a good visual composition and avoid placing important text too close to screen edges.
Use a real available font and robust text-rendering approach. Handle punctuation and text escaping safely in FFmpeg commands.
Never construct shell commands unsafely from user input.

9. Backend API and job management
Implement a clean API. Names can be adapted to the repository, but the equivalent functionality is required.
Suggested endpoints:
- GET /api/health — basic service status.
- GET /api/providers/status — status of configured providers without exposing secrets.
- POST /api/generations — validate inputs and create a generation job.
- GET /api/generations/{job_id} — return job state and available results.
- POST /api/generations/{job_id}/regenerate-copy — regenerate selected text using updated settings.
- POST /api/generations/{job_id}/regenerate-voiceover — regenerate narration when configured.
- GET /api/generations/{job_id}/assets/{asset_id} — securely retrieve a generated asset.
Use typed request and response models.
A job should have a state such as:
- queued
- generating_copy
- generating_video
- generating_voiceover
- assembling_video
- completed
- failed
Not every stage will run for every request, so voiceover-disabled jobs should skip that stage cleanly.
Persist enough job metadata to recover the results in local development. Do not put the generated MP4's binary contents into SQLite.
Use IDs rather than accepting arbitrary filesystem paths from clients.
Ensure errors are recorded in a useful, non-sensitive way.
For a short prototype, a simple background-task mechanism with polling is acceptable, provided it can handle the selected workflow. Document the limits of that approach and keep the processing layer modular enough to move into a dedicated worker later.

10. Data models
Define explicit, validated data structures for:
ProductInput
Contains product details, factual specifications, uploaded image reference, and optional brand voice.
CreativeSettings
Contains selected platform or platforms, tone, visual style, target audience, objective, duration, aspect ratio, and voiceover preference.
CopyOutput
Contains platform-specific titles, descriptions, bullets, captions, tags, keywords, SEO fields, CTA, video script, prompt, and warnings.
GenerationJob
Contains job ID, status, timestamps, selected settings, safe error information, and references to generated assets.
GeneratedAsset
Contains asset ID, media type, storage reference, duration when applicable, and generation method.
Keep schemas consistent between frontend and backend. Validate on the server even when the browser already validates.

11. Frontend design requirements
The application must look like a modern creative product, not an unstyled technical dashboard.
Use a restrained visual system:
- Light neutral background.
- Dark, legible typography.
- One strong accent color.
- Clear spacing and hierarchy.
- Good image previews.
- Rounded cards used purposefully.
- Consistent buttons and controls.
- Responsive layout.
- Accessible labels, focus states, contrast, and keyboard navigation.
Avoid excessive gradients, generic AI sparkle decorations everywhere, and placeholder charts.
Required screens
A. Home/workspace
- SellCraft AI branding.
- Short statement explaining the value.
- A visible “Create marketing kit” action.
- A small example or sample output if useful.
- A clear open-model/provider status area.
B. Product setup
- Product image upload.
- Product information fields.
- Platform selector.
- Tone, visual style, objective, and voiceover controls.
- Clear generation button.
C. Generation progress
- Real job status.
- Progress steps that correspond to backend processing.
- Retry and failure states.
D. Results editor
- Product listing section.
- Platform-specific content tabs or sections.
- Editable text.
- Copy and regenerate actions.
- Video preview.
- Voiceover preview when available.
- Download actions.
- Clearly stated video-generation method.
Do not make all controls tiny or squeeze the interface into one crowded form.

12. Security, privacy, and correctness
The app handles user-provided product images and business information.
Implement:
- File-type and size validation.
- Safe generated filenames.
- Protected asset retrieval.
- Server-side secret handling.
- Sensible request timeouts.
- API error handling.
- Temporary file cleanup.
- No arbitrary filesystem access through request parameters.
- No unsafe shell string interpolation.
Make it clear when a hosted inference provider will receive a product image. A local text model does not mean the entire pipeline is local if image-to-video or text-to-speech is hosted.
Do not log API keys or unnecessarily log complete product descriptions.
Use an appropriate temporary-file and output-cleanup strategy. For deployment, account for ephemeral storage and do not assume local files automatically persist across restarts.

13. Testing and quality assurance
Add practical tests for:
- Input validation.
- Missing product facts.
- Structured output validation.
- Prompt generation.
- Provider unavailable errors.
- Failed video generation.
- Optional voiceover disabled.
- Job status transitions.
- Invalid image upload.
- MP4 assembly and duration validation when FFmpeg is installed.
- Download and asset authorization behavior.
Use mocks for unit tests. Never require live paid APIs for the default test suite.
Add at least one end-to-end test or repeatable manual acceptance test that validates the core flow.
The application is not complete merely because the page loads. The input, generation, results, and download workflow must work end-to-end.

14. Documentation and repository deliverables
Create:
- README.md with a clear project overview, setup steps, architecture, provider configuration, limitations, and demo instructions.
- .env.example with placeholders only.
- Backend dependency file such as requirements.txt or pyproject.toml.
- Frontend dependency files.
- A clear directory structure.
- Unit tests.
- Instructions for Ollama and the selected language model.
- Instructions for configuring ElevenLabs.
- Instructions for enabling the real image-to-video provider.
- A description of animated-photo fallback behavior.
- The applicable AI model and dependency license references.
Do not commit model weights, uploaded product files, generated videos, database files, or secrets.
Document the distinction between open-weight model inference and commercial third-party services.

15. Out of scope for this MVP
Do not implement these unless the core workflow is already working and tested:
- User authentication.
- Subscriptions or payment integration.
- Automatic publishing to social platforms.
- A marketplace.
- A complex multi-user product catalog.
- Fine-tuning infrastructure.
- Unnecessary agent frameworks.
- Unverified claims of guaranteed SEO rankings or increased sales.
- Many different video model integrations.
- Fake analytics or fabricated performance results.
The goal is a focused, real product that can be demonstrated to one actual seller.

16. Definition of done
The project is ready for demonstration when all of the following are true:
1. A user can upload a product photo and enter product facts.
2. A user can choose the target platform, tone, visual style, and objective.
3. The open-weight language-model integration generates structured, editable product copy.
4. Missing or uncertain facts are not silently invented.
5. The user can regenerate an individual text section.
6. A valid 10-second MP4 can be produced through a real configured video model or the explicitly labelled animated-photo fallback.
7. ElevenLabs narration works when credentials are configured, and the app continues gracefully without it.
8. The result page previews and downloads the assets.
9. Errors and progress states are truthful and understandable.
10. The app can be installed and run by following the README.
11. Tests for the important code paths pass.
12. No API keys or private credentials are present in the repository.
17. Implementation instructions to you, the coding agent
Begin by inspecting the current repository and identifying the framework, files, and any existing working features.
Then:
1. Write a concise implementation plan based on the actual repository.
2. Establish the core runnable application.
3. Implement product input and creative controls.
4. Implement open-weight text generation and structured output validation.
5. Implement results editing.
6. Implement media-job orchestration and the FFmpeg fallback.
7. Add a real image-to-video adapter for a verified configured runtime.
8. Add ElevenLabs voice generation.
9. Add final video assembly, preview, and downloads.
10. Add tests, error handling, .env.example, and README documentation.
11. Run the available build, type checks, linting, and tests. Fix errors that you can reproduce.
12. Summarize the files changed, commands used, tests run, current limitations, and exact run instructions.
Prioritize a working end-to-end path over architectural complexity. Make sensible engineering decisions without stopping for unnecessary clarification.
If a feature cannot be completed because an external service, credential, GPU, or model checkpoint is unavailable, finish the remaining workflow, provide an honest fallback, document the missing configuration, and do not claim that unavailable integration was tested.
Start by inspecting the repository, then build SellCraft AI.




10. What I recommend you actually build first
The prompt above describes the product's direction, but don't let the coding agent spend all its time wiring up complicated video inference before the core experience exists.
Use this implementation order:
1. Product form → open-weight copy generation → editable results.
2. A real 10-second MP4 using FFmpeg, with an option to use genuine image-to-video inference where the runtime is available.
3. ElevenLabs voiceover and final audio/video assembly.
4. Polish the interface, test with one real seller, and record the demo.
This gives you a runnable product early, while preserving the more impressive generative-video path.

## 4. Backend module / class diagram (UML-ish)

```

  │◄────────────┤ results: copy + video + audio + downloads
```

## 8. API surface

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| GET | /api/health | liveness |
| GET | /api/providers/status | ollama/model, ffmpeg, video provider, elevenlabs (no secrets) |
| POST | /api/uploads | multipart image → asset_id |
| POST | /api/generations | create job |
| GET | /api/generations/{id} | status + results |
| PATCH | /api/generations/{id}/copy | save user edits |
| POST | /api/generations/{id}/regenerate-copy | section/tone regenerate (no video rerun) |
| POST | /api/generations/{id}/regenerate-voiceover | TTS + re-assemble only |
| GET | /api/generations/{id}/assets/{asset_id} | protected download (ID lookup, job-scoped) |
| GET | /api/voices | permitted ElevenLabs voices |

```
 0s──2s────────6s──────8s────10s
 │Hook │ Showcase │ Key  │ CTA  │   zoom/pan on photo (fallback) or LTX motion

 └─────┴──────────┴──────┴──────┘   audio: ElevenLabs narration (optional) + loudnorm
```
Fallback: blurred-bg + fitted product (no stretch), zoompan, drawtext/ASS, safe margins. Output H.264 + AAC, ffprobe-verified 9.5–10.5s.

## 10. Directory structure

```
sellcraft/
 ├─ README.md  .env.example  .gitignore  docker-compose.yml(optional)
 ├─ backend/  pyproject|requirements.txt
 │   ├─ app/ main.py config.py db.py
 │   │   ├─ api/ (health, providers, uploads, generations, assets)
 │   │   ├─ schemas/ (product, settings, copy, job, asset)
 │   │   ├─ services/ (llm/, video/, tts/, assembly/, jobs/, storage/, prompts/)
 │   │   └─ core/ (errors, logging, security)
 │   ├─ data/ (uploads, outputs, sellcraft.db)  ← gitignored
 │   └─ tests/
 ├─ frontend/ package.json app/ components/ lib/ tests/
 └─ docs/ (architecture, demo script, license notes)
```

## 11. Security / privacy checklist
Backend-only keys · MIME+magic-byte check, ≤10 MB, JPEG/PNG/WebP · UUID filenames · asset access by ID scoped to job · FFmpeg via argv list (no shell) + text sanitised/escaped · no prompt/product text in logs · CORS locked to frontend origin · cleanup of old uploads/outputs · README states what leaves the device (hosted LTX = image sent; ElevenLabs = script sent; Ollama = local).

## 12. Hacktoberfest prize mapping (pick, don't spread thin)
Main prize ($250): Writing Quality + open-weight story. Realistic add-ons:
- **Best Use of Gemma** ($200) — Gemma via Ollama ✔ native fit
- **Best Use of ElevenLabs** ($100) — voiceover ✔ native fit
- Optional cheap wins: Entire/DevRelay session share ($100), .tech domain (needs deploy), Render (needs GPU/host), Temporal (extra work — skip unless time)

## 13. Risks & mitigations
| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| 3-day deadline | Strict build order; video AI is optional |
| No GPU for LTX | Fallback is first-class; label honestly; LTX adapter documented as "untested" unless run |
| Gemma returns bad JSON | JSON-schema `format`, Pydantic, 1 repair retry, error surfacing |
| Hallucinated claims | Strict system prompt + `missing_information` + `claims_requiring_review` + forbidden-words post-check |
| FFmpeg font/escaping bugs | Bundled font file, textfile= input, argv list |
| Scope creep (5-platform "all" mode) | Single LLM call per platform, one shared video |
| Writing-quality weighting | Reserve final half-day for DEV post + real-user feedback |

## 14. Open questions for you (confirm before coding)
1. Gemma size your machine can run (RAM)? Is Ollama/ffmpeg already installed?
2. Do you have an ElevenLabs key?
3. Any GPU / hosted endpoint for LTX, or fallback-only demo?
4. Pure local demo, or deploy (Render/DO)?
5. Do you have a real seller lined up for the "first user" bonus?

## Verification (once coding starts)
`pytest` (mocks), `ffprobe` on output = ~10s, `npm run build` + `tsc`, manual E2E: upload → generate → edit → regen tone (video unchanged) → download MP4/MP3 → provider-offline error message check.

## 11. Security / privacy checklist
Backend-only keys · MIME+magic-byte check, ≤10 MB, JPEG/PNG/WebP · UUID filenames · asset access by ID scoped to job · FFmpeg via argv list (no shell) + text sanitised/escaped · no prompt/product text in logs · CORS locked to frontend origin · cleanup of old uploads/outputs · README states what leaves the device (hosted LTX = image sent; ElevenLabs = script sent; Ollama = local).

## 12. Hacktoberfest prize mapping (pick, don't spread thin)
Main prize ($250): Writing Quality + open-weight story. Realistic add-ons:
- **Best Use of Gemma** ($200) — Gemma via Ollama ✔ native fit
- **Best Use of ElevenLabs** ($100) — voiceover ✔ native fit
- Optional cheap wins: Entire/DevRelay session share ($100), .tech domain (needs deploy), Render (needs GPU/host), Temporal (extra work — skip unless time)

## 13. Risks & mitigations
| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| 3-day deadline | Strict build order; video AI is optional |
| No GPU for LTX | Fallback is first-class; label honestly; LTX adapter documented as "untested" unless run |
| Gemma returns bad JSON | JSON-schema `format`, Pydantic, 1 repair retry, error surfacing |
| Hallucinated claims | Strict system prompt + `missing_information` + `claims_requiring_review` + forbidden-words post-check |
| FFmpeg font/escaping bugs | Bundled font file, textfile= input, argv list |
| Scope creep (5-platform "all" mode) | Single LLM call per platform, one shared video |
| Writing-quality weighting | Reserve final half-day for DEV post + real-user feedback |

# SellCraft AI — Project Plan

**Tagline:** One product photo. A few facts. A complete marketing kit.
**Event:** Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge, Week 2 — *Side Hustle*. Submissions due **Oct 18, 2026**.
**Status:** Planning complete. Verdict: **GO** (scope-cut MVP).

> **Scope decision:** ElevenLabs voiceover is **deferred** (no free tier). The TTS layer stays behind an interface so it can be added later (ElevenLabs, or the open-source Piper). The MVP produces a **silent video with on-screen text/captions**; the voiceover script is still generated and editable as text.

---

## 1. What we're building
An AI marketing studio for small online sellers (Instagram, Etsy, Shopify, etc.). The seller uploads a product photo, enters a few verified facts, picks platform/tone/style/goal, and gets:

- Platform-specific listing copy (title, descriptions, bullets, tags, SEO, caption, CTA)
- A video-ad brief (hook, storyboard, motion prompt, on-screen text, voiceover script)
- A 10-second vertical (9:16) MP4 ad — real image-to-video model if available, otherwise an honestly-labelled **animated-photo ad** built with FFmpeg

The open-weight LLM (Gemma via Ollama) does the core content generation. It never invents facts; missing info is flagged.

**Not in MVP:** accounts, payments, auto-publishing, custom training, analytics, catalog manager, many video modes, voiceover (deferred).

## 2. Why open-source matters (for the DEV post)
- Copy generation runs **locally** on Gemma: seller product data stays on their machine, zero per-generation cost.
- Swappable model behind a provider interface (change `OLLAMA_MODEL`).
- Honest about what is not local (hosted video provider, if ever enabled).
- Targets prizes: **Best Use of Gemma** ($200) + main prize (writing quality weighted most).

## 3. System architecture

```
 ┌───────────────────────── BROWSER (Seller) ─────────────────────────┐
 │ Next.js (App Router) · TypeScript · Tailwind · shadcn/ui · Lucide  │
 │ Home/Status │ Product Form │ Creative Controls │ Progress │ Results│
 └───────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘
                                 │ HTTP/JSON + multipart (no secrets)
 ┌───────────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────────────┐
 │                FASTAPI BACKEND (Python, Pydantic)                  │
 │ API routers → Job Orchestrator (BackgroundTasks) → SQLite (jobs)   │
 │ Upload service (type/size/safe name)                               │
 │   1 CopyService     → OllamaProvider (open-weight, local)          │
 │   2 VideoService    → ImageToVideoProvider                         │
 │                        ├ AnimatedPhotoFallback (FFmpeg)  [default] │
 │                        └ LTXProvider (optional, GPU/hosted)        │
 │   3 TTSService      → (deferred) ElevenLabs / Piper                │
 │   4 AssemblyService → FFmpeg overlays + FFprobe validation         │
 │ Local file storage (UPLOAD_DIR / OUTPUT_DIR) + cleanup             │
 └──────┬───────────────────────┬──────────────────────┬──────────────┘
   ┌────▼─────┐          ┌──────▼──────┐        ┌──────▼─────┐
   │ Ollama   │          │ LTX-2/hosted│        │ FFmpeg /   │
   │ :11434   │          │ (optional)  │        │ FFprobe    │
   │ LOCAL    │          └─────────────┘        └────────────┘
   └──────────┘
```

## 4. Options per component

| Layer | Options | Chosen | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Frontend | **Next.js App Router**, Vite+React | Next.js | per spec |
| UI | **shadcn/ui + Tailwind**, Mantine | shadcn | accessible |
| Data fetching | **TanStack Query**, SWR | TanStack Query | job polling |
| Backend | **FastAPI**, Flask | FastAPI | Pydantic |
| Job runner | **BackgroundTasks**, ARQ/Redis, Celery, Temporal | BackgroundTasks | documented limit; modular for worker later |
| DB | **SQLite**, Postgres, MongoDB | SQLite | job metadata only |
| LLM runtime | **Ollama**, llama.cpp, vLLM | Ollama | local |
| LLM model | **Gemma 3 (4B/12B)**, Llama, Qwen | Gemma (size by RAM) | verify tag with `ollama list` |
| Structured output | **Ollama JSON-schema `format` + Pydantic + 1 repair retry** | same | |
| Image→video | **FFmpeg fallback**, LTX-Video/LTX-2, hosted GPU | Fallback default, LTX adapter behind flag | label honestly |
| TTS | ElevenLabs, Piper | **Deferred** | interface stubbed, UI shows "not configured" |
| Assembly | **FFmpeg (argv list, no shell)**, MoviePy | FFmpeg | |
| Storage | **Local FS**, S3/R2 | Local FS | ephemeral on deploy |
| Tests | **pytest + httpx + mocks**, Vitest/Playwright | pytest + manual E2E script | |
| Hosting | **Local**, Render, DigitalOcean | Local demo first | |

## 5. Backend design

**Provider interfaces**
- `LLMProvider`: `health()`, `generate_json(prompt, schema)` → `OllamaProvider` (+ visibly-labelled `DemoProvider` when Ollama is offline)
- `ImageToVideoProvider`: `available()`, `generate(image, motion_prompt, duration, aspect, ctx)` → `AnimatedPhotoFallbackProvider`, `LTXProvider`
- `TTSProvider` (stub only in MVP): `available()`, `voices()`, `synthesize()`

**Prompt structure** (separate sections): `FACTS | PLATFORM | TONE | STYLE | OBJECTIVE | RULES | OUTPUT SCHEMA`.
Rules: facts are the only source of truth; never invent specs, prices, discounts, reviews, certifications, "eco/organic/handmade/hypoallergenic" claims; flag gaps in `missing_information`; list risky phrasing in `claims_requiring_review`; honour the seller's forbidden words (post-check enforced in code).

**Job states:** `queued → generating_copy → generating_video → assembling_video → completed` (or `failed`). `generating_voiceover` exists in the enum but is skipped in MVP. Copy-only regeneration never re-runs video.

**Data models (Pydantic):** `ProductInput`, `CreativeSettings`, `CopyOutput` (+ per-platform outputs), `GenerationJob`, `GeneratedAsset`.
Enums — Platform: instagram/facebook/pinterest/etsy/shopify · Tone: straightforward/persuasive/emotional/friendly/luxury/playful · Style: premium_studio/ugc/minimal/warm_cozy/bold_colorful · Objective: sales/awareness/gift/features.

**API**

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| GET | /api/health | liveness |
| GET | /api/providers/status | ollama/model, ffmpeg, video provider (no secrets) |
| POST | /api/uploads | validated image → asset_id |
| POST | /api/generations | create job (202) |
| GET | /api/generations/{id} | status + results |
| PATCH | /api/generations/{id}/copy | save user edits |
| POST | /api/generations/{id}/regenerate-copy | section/tone regen, no video rerun |
| GET | /api/generations/{id}/assets/{asset_id} | protected download |

**Security:** magic-byte + MIME check, ≤10 MB, JPEG/PNG/WebP; UUID filenames; asset access by ID scoped to job; FFmpeg via argv list + sanitized text (use `textfile=`); no product text or secrets in logs; CORS locked; periodic cleanup.

## 6. Video pipeline (10 s, 9:16, 1080×1920)

```
 0–2s Hook │ 2–6s Product showcase │ 6–8s Key verified feature │ 8–10s CTA (name + CTA)
```
Fallback: blurred background + fitted product (no stretching), gentle zoom/pan, drawtext with a bundled font, safe margins, burned-in captions. Export H.264 (+AAC only if audio exists). FFprobe must confirm ≈10 s (9.5–10.5) or the job fails. UI/API label: **"Animated-photo ad"** vs **"AI-generated video (LTX)"**. LTX adapter only claimed as working if actually run.

## 7. Frontend design

```
app/
 ├ page.tsx            Home: hero, provider-status badge, "Create marketing kit"
 ├ create/page.tsx     ProductForm (+ImageDropzone) · CreativeControls · Generate
 └ jobs/[id]/page.tsx  ProgressStepper (real backend state) → ResultsWorkspace
      CopyTabs (per platform, editable, copy, regenerate)
      ToneRegenerate · WarningsPanel (missing info / claims to review)
      VideoPlayer + MethodBadge · DownloadBar (MP4, listing .txt/.json)
      Voiceover script panel (text only, fit-in-10s estimate)
```
Style: light neutral background, dark text, one accent color, rounded cards used purposefully, responsive, accessible focus states.

## 8. Directory structure

```
sellcraft/
 ├ plan.md  README.md  .env.example  .gitignore
 ├ backend/  requirements.txt
 │   ├ app/ main.py config.py db.py
 │   │   ├ api/  schemas/  core/
 │   │   └ services/ llm/ video/ tts/ assembly/ jobs/ storage/ prompts/
 │   ├ data/ (uploads, outputs, db — gitignored)
 │   └ tests/
 ├ frontend/ (Next.js app)
 └ docs/ (architecture, demo script, licenses)
```

## 9. Config (`.env.example`, placeholders only)
`OLLAMA_BASE_URL` `OLLAMA_MODEL` `VIDEO_PROVIDER` (`fallback`|`ltx`) `VIDEO_PROVIDER_URL` `VIDEO_PROVIDER_API_KEY` `UPLOAD_DIR` `OUTPUT_DIR` `DATABASE_URL` · (later) `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` `ELEVENLABS_DEFAULT_VOICE_ID`

## 10. Milestones (deadline Oct 18)

| Day | Goal | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| **Day 1 (Oct 15–16)** | Scaffold + product form → Gemma copy → editable results | Real structured copy from local Gemma; edit/copy/regenerate section & tone |
| **Day 2 (Oct 16–17)** | FFmpeg animated-photo MP4 + assembly + preview/download | ffprobe-verified ~10 s MP4 with overlays, labelled correctly |
| **Day 3 (Oct 17–18)** | Polish, tests, README, real-seller test, DEV post | Tests pass; README run-through works; post submitted |
| Stretch | LTX adapter, ElevenLabs/Piper voiceover, Render deploy | only if time/GPU/credits |

## 11. Testing
pytest with mocks (never live paid APIs): input validation, missing facts, structured-output validation, prompt building, Ollama-offline error, failed video, job state transitions, invalid upload, FFmpeg assembly + duration (if installed), asset authorization. Plus one repeatable manual E2E script.

## 12. Risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| 3-day deadline | strict order; video AI optional |
| No GPU | fallback is first-class and honestly labelled |
| Bad JSON from Gemma | schema `format`, Pydantic, one repair retry, clear errors |
| Hallucinated claims | strict prompt + `missing_information` + forbidden-word check |

## 13. Prize focus
Main ($250, writing weighted most) · **Best Use of Gemma** ($200). Optional: Entire/DevRelay session share. ElevenLabs/Render/Temporal categories skipped for now.

## 14. Definition of done (MVP)
1. Upload photo + facts. 2. Choose platform/tone/style/objective. 3. Gemma generates structured, editable copy. 4. Missing facts flagged, not invented. 5. Regenerate a single section/tone without touching video. 6. Valid ~10 s MP4 (labelled animated-photo ad unless a real model ran). 7. Preview + download. 8. Truthful progress/errors. 9. README setup works. 10. Tests pass. 11. No secrets committed.

- Gemma size / RAM and whether Ollama + ffmpeg are installed (to be checked at scaffold time).

## 7b. Mobile-first requirements (demo will be shown on a phone)

**Principle:** design for ~390px width first, then scale up to desktop. The phone is the primary demo device.

**Layout & UX**
- Single-column, one-step-at-a-time wizard on mobile (Product → Style → Generate → Results); side-by-side panels only at `md:` and up.
- Touch targets ≥ 44×44 px; segmented controls become horizontally scrollable chips or bottom-sheet pickers; sticky bottom "Generate" / "Download" bar.
- No horizontal page scroll; use `100dvh` (not `100vh`), safe-area insets (`env(safe-area-inset-*)`), and viewport meta `width=device-width, initial-scale=1`.
- Inputs use ≥16px font (prevents iOS zoom-on-focus) and proper `inputMode`/`autocomplete`.
- Results: tabs collapse to a scrollable tab bar; copy buttons give instant "Copied" feedback (Clipboard API with fallback).
- Respect `prefers-color-scheme`/reduced motion; keep the UI light and fast (no heavy JS, lazy-load the video).

**Photo input**
- `<input type="file" accept="image/jpeg,image/png,image/webp" capture="environment">` option so the seller can **take a photo with the phone camera** or pick from the gallery.
- Handle large phone photos: client-side downscale (max ~2048px, re-encode) before upload, server still validates type/size; handle HEIC by converting client-side or showing a clear "use JPEG/PNG/WebP" message.

**Video on mobile**
- `<video playsinline controls muted preload="metadata">` with a poster frame; vertical 9:16 fits the phone screen natively.
- Export H.264, `-pix_fmt yuv420p`, `-movflags +faststart`, even dimensions → plays in iOS Safari and Android Chrome.
- Download: use `<a download>` plus the Web Share API (`navigator.share({files})`) as the "Save / Share" path, since iOS often ignores direct downloads.

**Reaching the app from the phone (demo setup)**
- Run Next.js with `-H 0.0.0.0` and FastAPI on `0.0.0.0`; the phone opens `http://<laptop-LAN-IP>:3000` on the same Wi-Fi. Next `rewrites` proxy `/api/*` to FastAPI so the phone only talks to one origin (no CORS/mixed-content issues).
- Ollama and FFmpeg stay on the laptop; the phone is just the UI.
- Fallback if Wi-Fi blocks device-to-device traffic (e.g. college/venue networks): a tunnel such as `cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:3000` (HTTPS also needed for camera access/Clipboard/Share on some browsers). Document both in the README.
- Camera capture and `navigator.share` require a secure context on some browsers → plan on the HTTPS tunnel for the camera part of the demo.

**Testing for mobile**
- Manual checklist on a real iPhone Safari and Android Chrome: upload from camera, form usability with keyboard open, progress screen, video playback, copy, share/save.
- Playwright run with a mobile viewport (e.g. iPhone 14 / Pixel 7 device profiles) for the core flow.
- Optional: make it installable as a PWA (manifest + icons) so it opens full-screen from the home screen for the demo; no offline mode needed.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS assets (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  job_id TEXT,
  kind TEXT NOT NULL,
  mime TEXT NOT NULL,
  method TEXT,
  duration_seconds REAL,
  path TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL
);
"""


def now() -> datetime:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc)


def new_id() -> str:
    return uuid.uuid4().hex


@contextmanager
def connect():
    path = get_settings().db_path
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path, timeout=30)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    try:
        yield conn
        conn.commit()
    finally:
        conn.close()


def init_db() -> None:
    with connect() as c:
        c.executescript(SCHEMA)


def _asset(row: sqlite3.Row) -> GeneratedAsset:
    return GeneratedAsset(
        id=row["id"], kind=row["kind"], mime=row["mime"], method=row["method"],
        duration_seconds=row["duration_seconds"],
        created_at=datetime.fromisoformat(row["created_at"]),
    )


def _job(row: sqlite3.Row, assets: list[GeneratedAsset]) -> GenerationJob:
    return GenerationJob.model_validate({
        "id": row["id"],
        "status": row["status"],
        "created_at": row["created_at"],
        "updated_at": row["updated_at"],
        "product": json.loads(row["product"]),
        "settings": json.loads(row["settings"]),
        "copy_output": json.loads(row["copy_output"]) if row["copy_output"] else None,
        "copy_source": row["copy_source"],
        "error": json.loads(row["error"]) if row["error"] else None,
        "stages": json.loads(row["stages"]),
        "assets": [a.model_dump() for a in assets],
    })


def create_job(product, settings) -> str:
    job_id = new_id()
    ts = now().isoformat()
    with connect() as c:
        c.execute(
            "INSERT INTO jobs (id,status,created_at,updated_at,product,settings) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?)",
            (job_id, JobStatus.queued.value, ts, ts, product.model_dump_json(), settings.model_dump_json()),
        )
    return job_id


def get_job(job_id: str) -> GenerationJob | None:
    with connect() as c:
        row = c.execute("SELECT * FROM jobs WHERE id=?", (job_id,)).fetchone()
        if not row:
            return None
        assets = [_asset(r) for r in c.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM assets WHERE job_id=? ORDER BY created_at", (job_id,))]
    return _job(row, assets)


def update_job(job_id: str, **fields) -> None:
    """fields: status, copy_output (model|None), copy_source, error (model|None), stages (list of models)."""
    cols, vals = ["updated_at"], [now().isoformat()]
    for k, v in fields.items():
        if k == "status":
            v = v.value if hasattr(v, "value") else v
        elif k in ("copy_output", "error"):
            v = v.model_dump_json() if v is not None else None
        elif k == "stages":
            v = json.dumps([s.model_dump(mode="json") for s in v])
        cols.append(k)
        vals.append(v)
    with connect() as c:
        c.execute(f"UPDATE jobs SET {', '.join(f'{c_}=?' for c_ in cols)} WHERE id=?", (*vals, job_id))


def add_asset(*, kind, mime, path, method=None, duration_seconds=None, job_id=None, asset_id=None) -> str:
    asset_id = asset_id or new_id()
    with connect() as c:
        c.execute(
            "INSERT INTO assets (id,job_id,kind,mime,method,duration_seconds,path,created_at) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)",
            (asset_id, job_id, kind, mime, method, duration_seconds, str(path), now().isoformat()),
        )
    return asset_id


def get_asset_row(asset_id: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:
    with connect() as c:
        return c.execute("SELECT * FROM assets WHERE id=?", (asset_id,)).fetchone()


def attach_asset(asset_id: str, job_id: str) -> bool:
    """Attach an unattached upload to a job. Returns False if missing or already owned."""
    with connect() as c:
        cur = c.execute("UPDATE assets SET job_id=? WHERE id=? AND job_id IS NULL", (job_id, asset_id))
        return cur.rowcount == 1

import io
from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import UploadFile
from PIL import Image, ImageOps, UnidentifiedImageError

from .. import db
from ..config import get_settings
from ..errors import AppError

ALLOWED = {"JPEG": ("image/jpeg", "jpg"), "PNG": ("image/png", "png"), "WEBP": ("image/webp", "webp")}
MAX_PIXELS = 40_000_000


def save_upload(file: UploadFile) -> dict:
    """Validate by content (not filename/header), re-encode, store under a generated name."""
    s = get_settings()
    max_bytes = s.max_upload_mb * 1024 * 1024
    data = file.file.read(max_bytes + 1)
    if not data:
        raise AppError("empty_file", "The uploaded file is empty.")
    if len(data) > max_bytes:
        raise AppError("file_too_large", f"Image is larger than {s.max_upload_mb} MB.", status=413)
    try:
        with Image.open(io.BytesIO(data)) as probe:
            fmt = probe.format
            if probe.width * probe.height > MAX_PIXELS:
                raise AppError("image_too_large", "Image dimensions are too large.")
        if fmt not in ALLOWED:
            raise AppError("unsupported_type", "Use a JPEG, PNG or WebP image.", status=415)
        img = ImageOps.exif_transpose(Image.open(io.BytesIO(data)))
        img.load()
    except (UnidentifiedImageError, OSError, Image.DecompressionBombError):
        raise AppError("invalid_image", "That file isn't a valid JPEG, PNG or WebP image.", status=415)

    mime, ext = ALLOWED[fmt]
    if fmt == "JPEG" and img.mode != "RGB":
        img = img.convert("RGB")
    asset_id = db.new_id()
    dest: Path = s.upload_path / f"{asset_id}.{ext}"
    dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    img.save(dest, format=fmt, **({"quality": 92} if fmt == "JPEG" else {}))
    db.add_asset(kind="image", mime=mime, path=dest, method="upload", asset_id=asset_id)
    return {"asset_id": asset_id, "width": img.width, "height": img.height, "mime": mime}


def asset_file(row) -> Path:
    """Resolve an asset row to a file, refusing anything outside the managed directories."""
    s = get_settings()
    p = Path(row["path"]).resolve()
    for root in (s.upload_path.resolve(), s.output_path.resolve()):
        if p.is_relative_to(root) and p.is_file():
            return p
    raise AppError("asset_missing", "Asset file not found.", status=404)

"""Job orchestration. Each stage updates real state in SQLite; the frontend polls it.
Runs inside FastAPI BackgroundTasks (threadpool): fine for a single-process prototype,
but jobs die with the process. Stage functions are independent so they can move to a worker later."""
import logging

from .. import db, tracing
from ..errors import AppError
from ..schemas import JobError, JobStatus, StageEntry
from .copy import CopyService

log = logging.getLogger("sellcraft.jobs")


def _set_stage(job_id: str, stages: list[StageEntry], name: str, status: str, detail: str | None = None) -> None:
    now = db.now()
    for s in stages:
        if s.name == name:
            s.status = status
            s.detail = detail
            s.finished_at = now if status != "running" else None
            break
    else:
        stages.append(StageEntry(name=name, status=status, detail=detail, started_at=now,
                                 finished_at=now if status != "running" else None))
    db.update_job(job_id, stages=stages)


def run_generation(job_id: str, copy_service: CopyService | None = None) -> None:
    job = db.get_job(job_id)
    if job is None:
        return
    stages: list[StageEntry] = []
    try:
        with tracing.span("job", "generation", job_id=job_id, platforms=len(job.settings.platforms)):
            # --- stage 1: copy ---
            db.update_job(job_id, status=JobStatus.generating_copy)
            _set_stage(job_id, stages, "copy", "running")
            svc = copy_service or CopyService()
            with tracing.span("llm", "copy.generate", model=getattr(svc.llm, "model", "demo")) as sp:
                result = svc.generate(job.product, job.settings)
                if sp is not None:
                    for k, v in result.usage.items():
                        sp.set_data(k, v)
            db.update_job(job_id, copy_output=result.copy, copy_source=result.source)
            _set_stage(job_id, stages, "copy", "done", result.source)

            # --- later phases plug in here: video, voiceover, assembly ---
            _set_stage(job_id, stages, "video", "skipped", "Video generation not enabled yet")

        db.update_job(job_id, status=JobStatus.completed)
    except AppError as e:
        _fail(job_id, stages, e.code, e.message, e.retryable)
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - never leak internals to the client
        log.exception("unexpected failure in job %s", job_id)
        _fail(job_id, stages, "internal_error", "Something went wrong on our side. Please retry.", True)


def _fail(job_id, stages, code, message, retryable):
    running = next((s for s in stages if s.status == "running"), None)
    if running:
        _set_stage(job_id, stages, running.name, "failed", code)
    db.update_job(job_id, status=JobStatus.failed, error=JobError(code=code, message=message, retryable=retryable))

    job_id = db.create_job(req.product, req.settings)

    if job.copy_output is None:

    db.update_job(job_id, copy_output=copy)

@router.post("/generations/{job_id}/regenerate-copy")

    job = _job_or_404(job_id)
    if job.copy_output is None or job.status in (JobStatus.queued, JobStatus.generating_copy):
        raise AppError("not_ready", "Copy isn't ready yet.", status=409)
    result = CopyService().regenerate(job.copy_output, job.product, job.settings,

    fields = {"copy_output": result.copy, "copy_source": result.source}
    db.update_job(job_id, **fields)
    if req.tone and req.tone != job.settings.tone:
        db.update_job(job_id, settings=None) if False else None
    return _job_or_404(job_id)


@router.get("/generations/{job_id}/assets/{asset_id}")

    row = db.get_asset_row(asset_id)
    if row is None or row["job_id"] != job_id:
        raise AppError("asset_not_found", "Asset not found.", status=404)
    return FileResponse(storage.asset_file(row), media_type=row["mime"])

import logging
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.exceptions import RequestValidationError
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse

from . import db, tracing
from .api.routes import router
from .config import get_settings
from .errors import AppError

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s")


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(_: FastAPI):
    s = get_settings()
    s.upload_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    s.output_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    db.init_db()
    tracing.init()
    yield


app = FastAPI(title="SellCraft AI", version="0.1.0", lifespan=lifespan)
app.add_middleware(CORSMiddleware, allow_origins=get_settings().cors_origins.split(","),
                   allow_methods=["*"], allow_headers=["*"])
app.include_router(router)


@app.exception_handler(AppError)
async def app_error(_: Request, e: AppError):
    return JSONResponse(status_code=e.status, content={"error": {"code": e.code, "message": e.message, "retryable": e.retryable}})


@app.exception_handler(RequestValidationError)
async def validation_error(_: Request, e: RequestValidationError):
    # Only field locations + messages: never echo submitted values back.
    fields = [{"field": ".".join(str(p) for p in err["loc"] if p != "body"), "message": err["msg"]} for err in e.errors()]
    return JSONResponse(status_code=422, content={"error": {"code": "validation_error", "message": "Please check the highlighted fields.", "fields": fields}})

---
title: allowedDevOrigins
description: Use `allowedDevOrigins` to configure additional origins that can request the dev server.
---

{/* The content of this doc is shared between the app and pages router. You can use the `<PagesOnly>Content</PagesOnly>` component to add content that is specific to the Pages Router. Any shared content should not be wrapped in a component. */}

Next.js blocks cross-origin requests to dev-only assets and endpoints during development by default to prevent unauthorized access.

To configure a Next.js application to allow requests from origins other than the hostname the server was initialized with (`localhost` by default), use the `allowedDevOrigins` config option.

`allowedDevOrigins` lets you set additional origins that can request the dev server in development mode. For example, to use `local-origin.dev` instead of only `localhost`, open `next.config.js` and add the `allowedDevOrigins` config:

```js filename="next.config.js"
module.exports = {
  allowedDevOrigins: ['local-origin.dev', '*.local-origin.dev'],
}
```

Only the [`hostname`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/URL/hostname) of the request's `Origin` header is matched against your entries. For a request from `http://local-origin.dev:3000/dashboard?tab=1`, that is `local-origin.dev`. The scheme, the port, the path, and the query string are ignored. Write your entries that way too, without `https://` and without a port.

A no-cors cross-site request, such as a script tag loading a dev asset, sends no `Origin` header. Those are matched on the `Referer` hostname instead.

Entries can also expand, through two wildcards: a `*` stands in for exactly one label of the hostname, and `**` for one or more. That is why the example above lists two entries, one for the bare hostname and one for its subdomains.

| Entry                 | Matches                                             | Does not match                                 |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `local-origin.dev`    | `local-origin.dev`                                  | `team.local-origin.dev`                        |
| `*.local-origin.dev`  | `team.local-origin.dev`                             | `local-origin.dev`, `team.eu.local-origin.dev` |
| `**.local-origin.dev` | `team.local-origin.dev`, `team.eu.local-origin.dev` | `local-origin.dev`                             |

Partial replacement is not supported. Write `*.local-origin.dev`, rather than `team-*.local-origin.dev`. Using `**` is only supported at the start of the pattern.

The dev server already allows `localhost`, its subdomains, and the hostname it was started with. Any other hostname needs an entry, such as a tunnel used for remote development:

```js filename="next.config.js"
module.exports = {
  allowedDevOrigins: ['*.tunnel.example.com'],
}
```

# SellCraft AI

*One product photo. A few facts. A complete marketing kit.*

Small-seller marketing studio: upload a product photo, enter a few verified facts, pick a platform / tone / style / goal, and get platform-specific listing copy plus a video-ad brief. Copy is written by an **open-weight model (Gemma) running locally through Ollama**, so product data never leaves your machine. See [`plan.md`](plan.md) for the full design.

**Status:** Phase 1 (form → Gemma copy → editable results) is working. Video (FFmpeg animated-photo ad), ElevenLabs voiceover and Sentry tracing are next.

## What runs where
| Part | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Copy generation | Local (Ollama + Gemma) | Open weights, no per-use cost. Check Gemma's terms before commercial use. |
| Video | Local FFmpeg (next phase) | Will be labelled "animated-photo ad", not AI-generated footage |
| Voiceover | ElevenLabs (cloud, optional) | Script is sent to ElevenLabs. Key stays on the backend. |

## Run it
Prereqs: Python 3.12, Node 20+, [Ollama](https://ollama.com), ffmpeg.

```bash
# 1. model
ollama pull gemma3:4b          # or gemma3:12b if you have the RAM

# 2. backend
cd backend
uv venv --python 3.12 .venv && uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -r requirements.txt   # or python3.12 -m venv + pip
cp ../.env.example .env        # then edit
.venv/bin/uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000

# 3. frontend (new terminal)
cd frontend && npm install && npm run dev -- -H 0.0.0.0
# open http://localhost:3000
```
No Ollama yet? Set `DEMO_MODE=true` in `backend/.env`. The UI then shows a visible **Demo Mode** label; output is deterministic sample text, not a model response.

### Open it on your phone (same Wi-Fi)
Find your Mac's IP (`ipconfig getifaddr en0`), then add it so Next allows it in dev: `DEV_ORIGINS=192.168.x.x npm run dev -- -H 0.0.0.0` and open `http://192.168.x.x:3000`. Camera capture and clipboard need HTTPS on some browsers: use `cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:3000`.

## Tests
`cd backend && .venv/bin/python -m pytest` (mocked LLM, no live services needed).

## Layout
`backend/` FastAPI + SQLite + Ollama provider · `frontend/` Next.js (App Router, Tailwind) · `plan.md` design and roadmap.

## Secrets
Keys live only in `backend/.env` (gitignored). Never commit them.

Phase 1 is built and pushed. It works end to end in Demo Mode, but I haven't tried it with a real model or on a phone yet.

Ollama isn't installed on your Mac, so the copy you'd see now is labelled sample text, not Gemma output.

**What works**
- **Frontend (Next.js, built for phones first):**
  - The create flow is two steps on mobile and side by side on desktop, with a sticky bottom Generate bar.
  - Photos can come from the camera or the library, and they're shrunk before upload.
  - The progress screen shows the real backend stages, with a retry on failure.
  - The results page has editable, copyable sections, per-section regenerate, and a tone rewrite that doesn't touch the video.
  - It also shows warnings for missing facts and claims to check, a voiceover length estimate, and listing downloads as `.txt` and `.json`.
- **Backend (FastAPI):**
  - Image uploads are checked by content, not just the filename.
  - Copy is generated through Ollama with a JSON schema, one repair retry, and a check for the seller's forbidden words.
  - Job state is stored in SQLite, assets are only served to the job that owns them, and Sentry tracing is wired in.
- **Checks:** The backend has 26 passing tests using a fake model. The frontend passes typecheck, lint and build. I ran upload → generate → fetch through the Next proxy against a live backend in Demo Mode. I didn't open the pages in a browser.

**Not built yet:** the FFmpeg video, ElevenLabs voiceover, the Tinker fine-tune, and the DEV post.

**Where I need your input**
1. **Install Ollama and Gemma**, so we can test the real model. Run these in the prompt:
   - `! brew install ollama`
   - `! ollama serve` (leave it running in another terminal)
   - `! ollama pull gemma3:4b`

   Your 18 GB of RAM can run `gemma3:12b` (better writing, slower). I'd test with 4b first, and I haven't checked that this model tag exists in Ollama's library.
2. **Look at the UI.** Run the backend and frontend (commands are in the README), open it on your iPhone, and tell me what feels off. In Demo Mode, set `DEMO_MODE=true` in `backend/.env`. The README also has the phone setup.
3. **Your ElevenLabs key** goes in `backend/.env` as `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY=...`. Don't paste it here.
4. **Sentry:** if you want the Sentry prize, create a free project and put its DSN in `SENTRY_DSN`.

Once Gemma is running, I'll test real generation and tune the prompts. Then I'll start the FFmpeg video, the part that makes the demo stand out.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Start backend + frontend + an HTTPS tunnel so the app opens on your phone over ANY network
# (works on cellular, venue Wi-Fi that blocks device-to-device traffic, and gives the
# secure context iOS needs for camera capture, clipboard and share).
# Usage: scripts/dev-phone.sh        (set DEMO_MODE=true to run without Ollama)
set -euo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
LOG="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/sellcraft-dev"; mkdir -p "$LOG"
PIDS=()
cleanup() { for p in "${PIDS[@]:-}"; do kill "$p" 2>/dev/null || true; done; }
trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM

command -v cloudflared >/dev/null || { echo "Install it first: brew install cloudflared"; exit 1; }

(cd "$ROOT/backend" && exec .venv/bin/uvicorn app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --reload) >"$LOG/api.log" 2>&1 &
PIDS+=($!)
(cd "$ROOT/frontend" && exec npm run dev -- -H 127.0.0.1) >"$LOG/web.log" 2>&1 &
PIDS+=($!)

echo "Waiting for the app..."
for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
  curl -fs http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/health >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 1
done
curl -fs http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/health >/dev/null || { echo "App didn't start. See $LOG/*.log"; exit 1; }

cloudflared tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:3000 --no-autoupdate >"$LOG/tunnel.log" 2>&1 &
PIDS+=($!)
URL=""
for _ in $(seq 1 40); do
  URL="$(grep -Eo 'https://[a-z0-9-]+\.trycloudflare\.com' "$LOG/tunnel.log" | head -1 || true)"
  [ -n "$URL" ] && break; sleep 1
done
[ -n "$URL" ] || { echo "No tunnel URL. See $LOG/tunnel.log"; exit 1; }

echo; echo "Open on your phone:  $URL"; echo
command -v qrencode >/dev/null && qrencode -t ANSIUTF8 "$URL"
echo; echo "Anyone with this link can reach the app while it runs. Ctrl+C to stop. Logs: $LOG"
wait
E
chmod +x scripts/dev-phone.sh
(DEMO_MODE=true timeout 75 scripts/dev-phone.sh > /tmp/sc-phone.out 2>&1 &) ; for i in $(seq 1 60); do grep -q trycloudflare /tmp/sc-phone.out 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 1; done; head -12 /tmp/sc-phone.out; U=$(grep -Eo 'https://[a-z0-9-]+\.trycloudflare\.com' /tmp/sc-phone.out | head -1); sleep 5; echo "--- via tunnel:"; curl -s -m 20 -w "\nhome %{http_code}\n" -o /dev/null $U/; curl -s -m 20 $U/api/providers/status

content.text:
The phone issue is fixed and pushed, and I tested it. The Ollama commands and the Sentry step are below.

**Phone access (camera/HTTPS and Wi-Fi blocking)**
- I installed `cloudflared` and `qrencode` with Homebrew and wrote `scripts/dev-phone.sh`.
- It starts the backend, the frontend and a tunnel, then prints an `https://…trycloudflare.com` link and a QR code. Scan the QR with your iPhone camera.
- HTTPS fixes the camera and copy blocking on iPhone. The tunnel also works on any Wi-Fi, including ones that block device-to-device traffic, and even on cellular.
- I ran it and fetched the home page and `/api/providers/status` through a tunnel link. Both worked. I haven't opened it on an actual phone.
- Run it with `scripts/dev-phone.sh` from the project folder, or `DEMO_MODE=true scripts/dev-phone.sh` before Ollama is set up. Your code edits still hot-reload on the phone.
- While it runs, anyone with the link can use the app, and the link changes each time. Stop it with Ctrl+C.

**Ollama commands, to paste in any terminal**
```
brew install ollama
brew services start ollama
ollama pull gemma3:4b
ollama list
```
`brew services start ollama` runs the server in the background, so you don't need a separate `ollama serve` tab. `ollama list` should show `gemma3:4b`. Once it does, tell me, and I'll test real generation.

**Sentry:** your second screenshot shows the DSN, so I didn't type it in myself, because I could misread a character.
1. Click **Copy DSN** on that Sentry page.
2. Run this in the project folder:
   ```
   cd ~/Desktop/sellcraft/backend && sed -i '' 's|^SENTRY_DSN=.*|SENTRY_DSN='"$(pbpaste)"'|' .env && grep -c "^SENTRY_DSN=https" .env
   ```
   It prints `1` if it worked.
3. Don't copy the sample code on that page. It sets `send_default_pii=True`, but our code keeps it off so product text isn't sent to Sentry. The Logs and Metrics boxes you ticked don't matter. Tracing is the important one.

The mobile app works well, and I fixed both problems from your screenshots. The fixes are pushed, but I haven't re-checked them on your phone.

**"haa" came from your own facts.** You typed "haa choco chips", and Gemma 4B copied it word for word into the description, caption, video hook and on-screen text. The model ignored my prompt rule against this, so I now strip filler words like "haa" and "umm" from your facts in code before they reach the model. A real generation after the fix had no "haa" in it. Real words like "hammock" are left alone.

**Text boxes cut off long copy.** The Social caption box on your phone clipped its last line. All text boxes now grow to fit their content. The new build is live at `https://warranty-pub-chain-push.trycloudflare.com`, but I only verified that part against my own re-run.

**Other things I saw in your screenshots:**
- Gemma 4B is weak at rule-following. On the same product it added "for kids", which you never said. It also pasted my style-guide wording into the storyboard, and the storyboard invented actions like "hand breaking the biscuit". This is a good case for the Tinker fine-tune. For the demo, `gemma3:12b` should follow rules better. It's about 8 GB and slower, and you'd install it with `ollama pull gemma3:12b`. Want me to try it?
- The storyboard text won't matter for the FFmpeg video, because that uses your photo with motion and text.
- The Listing, Social, platform and Video tabs, the warning box, the tone rewrite and dark mode all rendered correctly.

**One mistake on my side:** `git add -A` earlier committed `IMG_9683.PNG` and `IMG_9684.PNG` to your private GitHub repo. I've removed them and added `IMG_*` to `.gitignore`, but the two files are still in the commit history. The repo is private, so this is low risk. I can scrub the history with a force-push if you want. I haven't done that without asking.

**Next:** I'll build the FFmpeg video (the animated-photo ad), then Sentry. Say "go", or tell me to try the 12b model first.
